About Cornell Utilities Production

Cornell Utilities Production, within Energy and Sustainability, operate the University energy infrastructure system on a 24-hour, 365-days-per-year basis.  Production facilities include a combined heat and power facility which provides both the steam for heat and electricity for campus.  All the water for campus is provided by a university-owned potable water filtration plant.  Electricity from the local utility is fed through a university-owned electric substation. Central Utilities serves over 150 major buildings and nearly 14 million square feet on central campus.

The Opportunity

Are you a highly organized professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex problems, and takes pride in supporting teams that keep critical operations running? We're seeking an Assistant to the Director to serve as a trusted partner to senior leadership within Utilities Production, helping coordinate administrative operations, regulatory reporting, safety training programs, purchasing activities, and special projects that support essential campus infrastructure.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys balancing strategic coordination with hands-on execution, building relationships across diverse teams, and making a meaningful impact behind the scenes.

About the Role

As the Assistant to the Director, you will play a central role in supporting the Director, Plant Managers, Supervisors, and a broad team of union and non-union staff. You'll oversee office operations, coordinate complex schedules, coordinate budgets and contracts, organize training programs, support regulatory reporting, and serve as a key liaison across departments and external partners.

Success in this role requires exceptional organizational skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, discretion with confidential information, and the ability to balance multiple priorities in a dynamic operational environment.

What You'll Do

Lead Administrative Operations

Serve as a trusted administrative partner to the Director and leadership team.

Coordinate complex calendars and help resolve competing scheduling priorities.

Coordinate meetings, events, tours, travel arrangements, and training activities.

Prepare agendas, presentations, reports, meeting materials, and minutes.

Respond independently to a wide range of inquiries and requests with professionalism and discretion.

Support daily office operations and help create efficient processes and procedures.

Collaborate with colleagues across the organization to ensure seamless administrative support.

Support Budget and Business Operations

Partner with Finance and departmental leadership on budget planning and monitoring.

Track expenditures and assist with annual budget development.

Coordinate contract services and monitor associated expenses.

Prepare spreadsheets, reports, dashboards, and other business documents.

Support purchasing, inventory management, and procurement activities.

Coordinate Training and Safety Programs

Help administer the Utilities Production safety training program.

Coordinate required OSHA-related training and professional development opportunities.

Schedule instructor-led and online training sessions.

Monitor completion rates and maintain training records and metrics.

Assist with conference registrations, travel planning, and training-related logistics.

Data and Regulatory Reporting

Collect, organize, analyze, and maintain operational and regulatory data.

Prepare reports required by state and federal regulatory agencies.

Maintain documentation and records in support of compliance requirements.

Assist with utility production reporting, fuel tracking, emissions reporting, and budget-related reporting.

Ensure accuracy, consistency, and timely submission of critical information.

Coordinate Purchasing and Order Tracking

Serve as a resource for purchasing and receiving activities.

Source and order supplies, equipment, tools, and materials.

Track orders and monitor delivery timelines.

Coordinate service requests and work orders using established systems and processes.

Maintain inventory records and support operational readiness.

This position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the operations that power and sustain a world-class institution. You'll work alongside dedicated professionals in engineering, operations, sustainability, facilities management, and administration while helping support critical infrastructure and environmental stewardship initiatives.

We value collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and respect for every member of our community. Your ideas, expertise, and perspective will help strengthen our team and contribute to our collective success. If you're a highly organized professional who enjoys supporting leaders, improving processes, and making a meaningful impact every day, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your resume and cover letter today!

What We Need

A cover letter and resume outlining your interest and how your experience and goals align with the potential for mutual success in the role are required for consideration.

Associate degree and 4 years administrative office experience or equivalent combination. 

Excellent communication and organizational skills, detail oriented and the ability to manage multiple priorities and tasks. 

Excellent knowledge of Adobe, MS Word, Excel, SharePoint, PowerPoint and Filemaker Pro in order to create original reports, documents and data bases.

Must possess strong grammar and written skills to respond to and create original difficult and/or sensitive correspondences for the Plant. 

The desire to work in and learn about electric, steam, and chilled water production.

Ability to multi-task, work independently, display sound judgment for setting priorities and handling sensitive/confidential conversations and correspondence.

Ability to coordinate a variety of events with large groups both within and outside of the Energy & Sustainability department.

Flexible, creative in finding solutions, able to follow directions and anticipate the needs of the Central Energy Plant management team.

Experience working directly with people from various socioeconomic backgrounds.

It Would Be a Bonus if You Have Any of the Following

Knowledge of Cornell administrative systems.

College level courses in business, project management and/or environmental sciences.

Experience using Maximo and web content management.

Working knowledge and understanding of technology and utilities systems in a campus environment.

Project/program management experience a plus.

Experience using AI tools.

Important Notes About Applying

A cover letter and resume outlining your interest and how your experience and goals align with the potential for mutual success in the role are required for consideration.

This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. For the first 30 days, the successful candidate will be expected to work fully on-site for onboarding and initial training. After that, employees typically perform this role on-campus 4 days per week and remotely 1 day per week.

There is no relocation assistance available for this position.

There is no visa sponsorship available for this position.

Rewards and Benefits

This position is based in Ithaca, New York, on Cornell’s main campus, and is fully onsite.

Cornell receives national recognition as an award-winning workplace for our health, wellbeing, and sustainability.

Our benefits programs include comprehensive health care options, generous retirement contributions, access to wellness programs, and employee discounts with local and national retail brands. We invite you to follow this link to get more information about our benefits: Understand Your Benefits | Working at Cornell.

Our leave provisions include health and personal leave, three weeks of vacation and 13 holidays: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and an end of the year winter break from December 25-January 1. To offer greater flexibility for observing faiths and traditions we also offer two additional floating holidays. Learn more about our generous leave provisions: Holiday and Accrued Time Off | Working at Cornell

Cornell's impressive educational benefits include tuition-free Extramural Study and Employee Degree Program, tuition aid for external education, and Cornell Children's Tuition Assistance Program. Learn more about our extensive educational benefits: Education Benefits | Working at Cornell

Follow this link to learn more about the Total Rewards of Working at Cornell:

Total Rewards | Working at Cornell.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Relocation Assistance is not available for this position.  

Cornell is an equal opportunity employer. For more information, visit hr.cornell.edu/eeo.

Who We Are:

Thank you for your interest in Mueller Water Products, Inc.  

For more than 165 years, Mueller Water Products, Inc. has been building the future of water infrastructure. From lifesaving fire protection to data intelligence, we are committed to developing products and solutions that help cities and utilities deliver clean, safe drinking water to hundreds of millions of people across North America.   

Our purpose is to connect communities to water, life’s most essential resource, with exceptional, people solutions and products. Behind that purpose is a dedicated team, united by our shared values of respect, integrity, trust, inclusion and safety. With a vision to be the leader in water infrastructure solutions—solving challenges, enriching lives and safeguarding the future—we are making a positive impact that will last for generations.   

By joining Mueller, you become part of a dynamic team dedicated to excellence and innovation, working collaboratively to achieve meaningful results. We champion our people because when they succeed, our communities thrive. We invite you to learn more about career opportunities with us and consider submitting your application.  


Assembly I

Mueller Company, a subsidiary of Mueller Water Products and publicly traded company (NYSE: MWA) is the nation's leading manufacturer of flow control devices for the water and gas distribution industries and North America's largest and only full-line supplier of potable water distribution products.  

 

The Mueller Co Cleveland TN location is growing and has an opening for a Production Assembler I to join the location to support all operational training needs for the Plant including various analysis projects.  

  

SUMMARY  

 

The driving force behind our growth at Mueller is our people. The assembly position is a crucial part of our team and ensuring that we deliver quality to our customers.  

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS DUTIES/RESPONSIBLITIES 

 

Implementing training programs that connect employee with business goals 

Work Safely in the Manufacturing Production Environment. 

Follow detailed verbal / written assembly instructions, processes, and procedures. 

Read and understand customer work orders and assembly instructions. 

Prepare and assemble materials and parts in a manufacturing production environment. 

Move, process, and organize materials and manufactured products. 

Operate hand power tools, presses, mills, lathes, drills, lifts, control equipment efficiently and safely. 

Perform quality control checks and verification of work order specifications. 

Properly fill out basic forms, reports, and label products correctly. 

Communicates and works effectively with others. 

May provide hands on and verbal job function training to coworkers as needed. 

Report problems with quality, processes, equipment and materials to Production Supervisor. 

Maintains a clean and organized work area to facilitate manufacturing functions. 

May support other departments and areas as needed.  

 

 

 

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 

Experience with CNC machines is a plus, but not required. 

Welding experience is a plus, but not required. 

Forklift experience is a plus, but not required. 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS 

 

High school diploma or equivalent. 

Must have good written and oral communication skills. 

Must have 2+ years of Assembly or Machine Operation experience in a manufacturing/warehouse setting. 

 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

 

Ability to use hands to finger, handle, or feel. 

Ability to frequently sit, stand, walk, reach within hands and arm’s length, stoop, kneel, and crouch.  

Ability to lift and/or move 50 pounds, and up to 50 pounds. 

Specific vision requirements include close vision and color vision. 

Ability to use power tools, air tools and other vibratory tools. 

Ability to work from a standing position for extended periods of time. 

Ability to work around hot heavy machinery.  

Ability to work in an open warehouse environment, subject to seasonal weather (hot/cold) 

Must be able to function in a high-pressure production type environment.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

Functions as part of the dialysis health care team in providing safe and effective dialysis therapy for patients under the direct supervision of a licensed nurse in accordance with organization policies, procedures, and training and in compliance with regulations set forth by the corporation, state, and federal agencies. Responsible for the setup and operation of hemodialysis machines. Assist in the maintenance of a safe and clean working environment. Supports the organization commitment to the Quality Enhancement Program (QEP) and CQI Activities, including those related to patient satisfaction and actively participates in process improvement activities that enhance the likelihood that patients will achieve the organization Quality Enhancement Goals (QEP).

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Patient Related

Education:

Assist other health care members in providing patient specific detailed education regarding adequacy measures where appropriate - Online Clearance Monitoring (OLC), Adequacy Monitoring Program (AMP), Urea Kinetic Modeling (UKM), and regarding disease process/access.

Treatment:

Welcome assigned patients and inquire as to their wellbeing since their last treatment.

Evaluate vascular access for patency, perform vascular access cannulation, and perform administration of heparin as delegated or as allowed by state law.

Obtain necessary pre and post treatment vital signs and weight and perform vascular access evaluation pre- treatment

Initiate dialysis treatment according to prescribed orders including blood flow (QB) and dialysate flow (QD).         

Evaluate intradialytic problems and provide intervention as prescribed by physician order or as directed.   

Monitor patients’ response to dialysis therapy. 

Obtain vital signs prior to reinfusion; perform all relevant functions necessary for the discontinuation of treatment - document.       

Discontinue dialysis treatment according to established procedures and evaluate patient prior to termination of venous access - standing & sitting blood pressure

Obtain Hemostasis and apply appropriate dressings.   

Evaluate the patient prior to discharge.

Perform and record Pre and Post dialysis evaluation, weight, and vital signs with initial identification        

Responsible for calculating and entry of individual patients’ dialysis machine programming for Ultrafiltration (UF) goal; treatment time; and UF modeling as prescribed.          

Responsible for ensuring appropriate safety alarms are enabled, including Narrow Venous Limits, (NVL) 160.    

Record accurate and timely information regarding vital signs and treatment parameters onto the Hemodialysis Treatment Sheet with initial identification      

Responsible for accurate documentation of information related to patient treatment including completion of Hemodialysis Treatment Sheet and, if applicable, progress notes.         

Report any significant information and/or change in patient condition directly to the registered nurse or supervisor.

Observe patient and conduct machine safety checks according to facility policy. Report any change or unusual findings to the registered nurse or supervisor.

Perform and document any intervention for unusual patient status and document patients' response to intervention.

Evaluate patients’ vascular access during treatment including arterial and venous monitoring pressures, provide appropriate intervention as needed, document and report any unusual findings to the registered nurse or supervisor.

Obtain all prescribed laboratory testing and prepare specimens for collection.      

Ensure that all blood spills are immediately cleaned with appropriate disinfectant according to facility policy.       

Prepare, organize, and efficiently utilize supplies and equipment to prevent wastage.       

Monitors patients performing self-care under the supervision of RN.

Staff Related

Assists in training of applicable direct patient care staff on appropriate programs under the supervision of a nurse.

Education/Communication:

Follows all organization business policies, procedures and systems incorporated into training, including compliance with ethical business practices

Maintain environmental integrity and aesthetics - ensure all areas are safe and clean.

Clean and disinfect dialysis machine surface, chair, equipment, and surrounding area between treatments according to facility policy.

Conduct all tasks necessary for preparation for dialysis treatment and document where appropriate and perform all required pretreatment dialysis machine alarm testing including Pressure Holding (PHT).

Initiate Solution Delivery System (SDS) system.

RECORD KEEPING:

Complete and document ongoing participation in Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) activities.   

Enters all treatment data into the designated clinical application in an accurate and timely manner.            

Review treatment sheets for completeness, ensure nursing signatures are documented, and ensure 

omitted entries are completed or corrected by appropriate staff.

Prepare initial patient chart for admission and compile paperwork for appropriate placement in chart. 

Prepare/print lab requisitions for prescribed or stat Lab specimens according to laboratory destination.       

Collect, label, appropriately prepare and store lab samples according required laboratory specifications.      

Ensure collection of lab specimens by appropriate lab courier.

         

INFECTION CONTROL:

ABOUT WATERSHED

Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.



We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!




THE ROLE

We are looking for a customer-focused and analytically-minded person to join the Sustainability Data Advisory team in our Mexico City office on a fixed-term basis, starting in December 2026. This is a chance to join a core team at a growth-stage startup that works with the world's top companies to speed up their sustainability programs. You'll work directly with customers as a trusted advisor, leading measurement sessions and delivering advisory services that unlock the full value of our platform. You'll help customers get clear, reliable insight into their sustainability impact and reach their sustainability goals.


YOU WILL:

 - Advise sustainability teams at many of the world's top companies. You'll work directly with customers on how to measure actionable carbon and non-carbon footprints to reach sustainability goals and enable real reductions. The work ranges from scoping new measurements to in-depth methodology comparisons between footprints.

 - Deliver services that speed up customer success. You'll help customers set up their measurements to meet sustainability goals, act as a trusted partner in emissions verifications, and give specialized advice to improve their data and methodologies. You'll make sure customers get the most out of Watershed's platform, faster and more effectively than they could on their own.

 - Collaborate with science, engineering and product teams to build new measurement solutions and expand Watershed's sustainability intelligence layer.


YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU:

 - Have 2–4 years of experience in a consulting, solutions-engineering or other customer-facing role. You are excited to work directly with customers to help them set the foundation for world-class sustainability programs.

 - Have experience in sustainability-related fields, greenhouse gas accounting and/or ESG reporting.

 - Are an excellent verbal and written communicator. You can explain complex topics to technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Learn quickly and work well in ambiguity. You are organized, systematic and efficient, and you thrive in a high-volume environment.

 - Think clearly about complex problems and are comfortable using and speaking to data. You are meticulous and detail-obsessed.

 - Are passionate about solving climate change and excited to help do so at a fast-paced startup.

 - Have strong English proficiency.


FIXED-TERM DETAILS

 - Starts in December 2026.

 - Minimum commitment of 4 months, with a possible extension of up to 3 more months.

 - Fixed-term employees receive compensation and benefits similar to full-time Watershed employees, including daily lunch delivered in the Watershed office.

 - This role requires working in person in our Mexico City office 4 days per week.

   





   

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.



What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.



What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”: a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

Engineers in the team own the design and development of core features on the platform. Data protection-focused functionality centers around file interfaces, including related Endpoint Security System Extension interfaces. Job Description Summary
#LI-Remote 

This is a field-based and remote opportunity supporting a team. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role. Please only apply if this location is accessible for you. The expectation of working hours and travel (domestic and/or international) will be defined by the hiring manager.   

The Regional Director (RD), Access & Reimbursement is a field-based role that serves as the regional lead for Novartis Dermatology Novartis Patient Support (NPS) Access & Reimbursement field teams. RDs lead a team of diverse field access & reimbursement roles focused on supporting customers on all matters related to patient access to our evolving Dermatology portfolio. The RD will provide leadership, management and coaching, operations, compliance, and budget oversight for their aligned regions in support of aligned product(s) strategy and pre-specified business goals. The RD must maintain a national perspective in their decision-making, collaborate with other NPS and cross-functional RDs, and lead projects/initiatives at a national- and regional-level. RDs are responsible for linking business strategy with exquisite and compliant execution within their regions to deliver pre-specified impact for the Novartis Pharmaceutical Corporation (NPC). They are also responsible for consistent acceleration of appropriate pull through of aligned business objectives. RDs should consistently demonstrate openness for courageous conversations and performance management of their direct reports to enable and bolster a forward-thinking culture, while also driving overall business impact. 

RDs will partner closely with other Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (NPC) field and headquarter-based associates, including Customer Engagement (Sales) and Market Access, representing NPC with the highest integrity in accordance with NPC Values and Behaviors. RDs will also be required to coordinate and communicate cross-functionally within NPC (e.g., Patient Support Center, Customer Engagement, Marketing, Market Access, Public Affairs, State & Government Affairs, Trade, Specialty Pharmacy Account Management, and other applicable third-party affiliates). The scope and scale of the role will adapt to meet the expanding needs of Novartis in pursuit of enterprise impact.

 

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:  

• Attract, coach, and retain team of high performing Access & Reimbursement professionals. 

• Oversee the recruiting, interviewing, hiring, training, and staffing of their regional team. 

• Create and nurture a team culture that embodies NPC Values and Behaviors and drives innovation, performance, and reputation. 

• Pull through national strategy at a regional level to enable exquisite execution. Under the advisement of their manager, RDs also may be responsible for leading specific national strategies and tactic development. 

• Proactively anticipate and coach teams on how to address access hurdles impacting key customers and patients. 

• Integrate with NPC leadership and collaborate across multi-functional teams (NPS, Customer Engagement, Marketing, Market Access, Operations, Training, Legal, ERC, etc.) to ensure a collaborative and compliant approach to support regional field success. 

• Seek to identify challenges, escalations, and/or delay in treatment initiation and continuation; closely partner with all matrix team members to resolve such issues. 

• Maintain a deep understanding of NPC policies and requirements and perform all responsibilities with integrity and in a manner consistent with company guidance and policies, relevant state and federal laws and regulations, and prescribed Values and Behaviors. 

 Minimum Requirements:  

Education: Minimum of a bachelor’s degree; advanced degree preferred (Majors preferred: Sciences, Business, Pharmacy, and Healthcare). 

Minimum of 8 years in reimbursement, contract strategy, managed care, sales/marketing or related field roles. At least 2 years leading a regional or local team and managing and collaborating across multiple stakeholders. 

Experience working with highly complex practices and/or health systems to establish access and acquisition pathways. 

Strategic account management experience using a proactive approach to anticipate access hurdles impacting accounts and patient access. 

Deep expertise and experience integrating manufacturer-sponsored patient support programs. 

Experience with specialty products acquired through specialty pharmacy networks and through buy-and-bill process, including expertise in acquisition, billing and coding, claims processing, and reimbursement. 

Proven track record of building and motivating teams. 

Past success in execution of launch strategies and plans. 

Candidate must reside within territory, or within a reasonable daily commuting distance of X miles from the territory border. Ability to travel 60-80% over a broad geography is required, with the ability to drive and/or fly within the territory. Must have a valid driver’s license. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Expertise in therapeutic space, practice dynamics and common reimbursement and product program support-related needs (oncology and/or diagnostic experience). 

Strong capabilities in the areas of patient support services, market access, customer focus, ability to work cross-functionally, launch execution, excellent communication, and presentation skills.

The salary for this position is expected to range between $194,600, and $361,400 per year. 

The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors. 

Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards. 

US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves. 

Driving is an Essential Function of this Role: Meaning it is fundamental to the purpose of this job and cannot be eliminated. Because driving is an essential function of the role, you must have a fully valid and unrestricted driver’s license to be qualified for this role. The company provides reasonable accommodations for otherwise qualified individuals with medical restrictions if an accommodation can be provided without eliminating the essential function of driving.  

COVID-19 Vaccine Policy (customer-facing roles only): While Novartis does not require vaccination for COVID-19 or proof of a recent negative test result for COVID-19 at this time, employees working in customer-facing roles must adhere to and comply with customers’ (such as hospitals, physician offices, etc.) credentialing guidelines, which may require vaccination. As required by applicable law, Novartis will consider requests for reasonable accommodation for those unable to be vaccinated. This requirement is subject to applicable state and local laws and may not be applicable to employees working in certain jurisdictions. Please send accommodation requests to Eh.occupationalhealth@novartis.com  

For Field Roles with a Dedicated Training Period:  

The individual hired for this role will be required to successfully complete certain initial training, including home study, eight (8) or fewer hours per day and forty (40) or fewer hours per week.

Position Overview
Novelis is one of the world leaders in aluminum recycling and rolling and a leading sustainable aluminum solutions provider. Driven by our purpose of shaping a sustainable world together, we work alongside our customers to provide innovative solutions to the aerospace, automotive, beverage packaging and specialty markets. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Novelis has approximately 13,000 employees in 32 operating facilities on 4 continents.
Responsibilities & Qualifications
Procurement Project Analyst (Contract) is responsible for analyzing supplier and Novelis operational data to identify total cost of ownership opportunities, support cost savings initiatives, and help advance Vision 3x30 ROIC objectives. The role evaluates plant data, conducts technical benchmarking, develops should-cost models for key and critical suppliers, and manages supplier quality KPI reporting to support risk mitigation and continuous improvement within procurement. The role operates in a complex manufacturing procurement environment where accurate data analysis, technical understanding, and cross-functional collaboration are required to identify cost reduction, supplier quality, and risk mitigation opportunities. The incumbent gathers and connects data from multiple internal and external sources, including ERP systems, ETQ, data lake sources, supplier inputs, and plant-level operational information.

*This is a long-term contract position with an anticipated assignment timeframe of December 2026 through March 2027.

Responsibilities

Data Collection, Integration, and Analysis
Identify, collect, and connect data from multiple sources, including ERPs, ETQ, the data lake, and other relevant systems. Use this data to analyze plant performance, supplier inputs, and total cost of ownership opportunities.
Technical Benchmarking and Opportunity Identification
Collect external data and perform technical comparisons and benchmarking across plants to identify efficiencies, cost reduction opportunities, and risk mitigation actions. Validate opportunities through data-driven analysis and collaboration with relevant stakeholders.
Should-Cost Modeling
Work with collaborators to identify relevant suppliers for should-cost model development. Define the scope and purpose of each model, build models using cost equations, analyze cost drivers, break down costs into categories, and allocate costs to specific processes.
Cost Reduction and Supplier Risk Analysis
Validate should-cost models using real-world data and interpret results to identify potential price, specification, scope, or cost reduction opportunities. Support procurement and operations in identifying supplier quality and supply risk mitigation opportunities.
Dashboard, KPI, and Reporting Development
Identify relevant KPIs with input from operations and procurement. Create manual dashboards, implement automated models, and analyze dashboard outputs to identify supplier risk mitigation opportunities.
Communication and Leadership Reporting
Create reports using Excel, Power BI, PowerPoint, and other tools to communicate insights, drive continuous improvement, and report findings to collaborators and leadership. Prepare executive summaries and present information clearly and effectively.
RFA Process Support
Develop full knowledge of the Novelis RFA process and template. Create relevant RFAs based on data analysis activities and support technical evaluation of recommendations through data-driven analysis and presentations to leadership.
This role is expected to independently conduct detailed data analysis, develop technical models, validate opportunities, and recommend actions based on data-driven findings. The role does not have final decision-making authority over supplier selection, commercial commitments, or budget approval; however, it provides critical analytical input to support procurement, operations, and leadership decisions.
The role solves problems by collecting and connecting data from multiple sources, analyzing cost drivers, validating models with real-world data, and interpreting results to identify cost reduction and risk mitigation opportunities. The role requires the ability to convert technical, operational, and supplier data into practical recommendations for procurement and leadership decision-making.
The role is accountable for producing accurate analysis, reliable cost models, relevant dashboards, and actionable recommendations that support procurement savings, risk mitigation, supplier quality visibility, and continuous improvement. The role also supports the creation of RFAs and leadership presentations based on data analysis activities.
This role will report to the Project Manager, Senior Manager for NNA Procurement, and will work closely with procurement, operations, plant teams, leadership, and data and analytics partners. The successful candidate will collaborate across functions to identify supplier and cost improvement opportunities, validate plant-level data, support should-cost modeling, establish relevant KPIs, develop RFAs, and communicate findings and recommendations to leadership. The role will also engage with suppliers and external benchmarking sources as needed to support supplier quality reviews, cost-driver analysis, technical comparisons, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, operations, supply chain, or a related field
Candidates should have at least two years of experience in manufacturing processes or a large-scale manufacturing environment involving metals, scrap, or similar operations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and project management skills are required, along with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and present findings effectively.
Experience working with multiple MRP systems is required
Proficiency with Excel and data analytics and reporting tools

SAP and/or Coupa experience
Experience with the following is preferred: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Azure AI / Azure OpenAI, ChatGPT or comparable enterprise GenAI platforms, Oracle, Celonis or comparable process-mining technology

Job Description

The Team:

The Mechatronic Software Platform (MSP) organization enables GM’s Software Defined Vehicle by making sure controllers, benches, and development vehicles are correctly instrumented and ready for calibration and software work.

The instrumentation team operates across many microcontroller families, ECUs, and electrical architectures. We sit at the intersection of ECU hardware, infrastructure software, calibration, and integration, working with SWILs, calibrators, hardware teams, and tool suppliers to ensure measurement, calibration, and trace/debug tooling work reliably on SDV platforms.

The Role:

We are looking for a hands-on Instrumentation Integration Engineer to own SDV instrumentation integration for infrastructure software. This role is part of the Infrastructure Calibration & Release team. This is a doing role, focused on real benches and hardware across multiple microcontrollers and ECU variants. You will ensure controllers are properly instrumented, tools are configured correctly, and issues are found and fixed quickly so development, integration, and calibration can proceed without delay.

Who Thrives Here:

Engineers who like to be on the bench, hands-on with real hardware across many microcontrollers, ECUs, and electrical architectures.

People who become the go-to resource when calibration, measurement, trace, or A2L details go sideways.

Individuals who are organized, detail oriented, and able to manage many instrumentation variants and benches without losing rigor.

Teammates who communicate clearly, move with urgency, and keep SWILs, calibrators, and hardware teams aligned on what is ready and what is blocked.

What You’ll Do (Responsibilities):

Integrate and maintain instrumentation hardware (e.g., calibration add-on boards, high-speed measurement interfaces, trace pods, vertical adapter modules) on SDV controllers and benches.

Configure, debug, and support calibration and measurement workflows, including XCP on DoIP, A2L/A2ML content, DAQ/measurement setups, and ECU flashing.

Bring up and maintain SDV calibration and farm benches across multiple microcontrollers, ECUs, and electrical architectures, ensuring they are usable and reliable.

Troubleshoot instrumentation issues end-to-end: hardware wiring, schematics, connectors, licenses, tool versions, configuration files, and interface definitions.

Develop and maintain instrumentation documentation (e.g., SOR Appendix T, “Development Tool Requirements,” and “Bill of Design”) for SDV and VIP controller programs.

Work with external tool and hardware suppliers and internal ECU/DRE teams to resolve hardware constraints, tool defects, and integration gaps.

Provide practical coaching to SWILs, calibrators, and other engineers on required instrumentation hardware, tool versions, and configurations.

Use scripting and AI-assisted tools where appropriate to speed up troubleshooting, documentation, and risk write-ups so decisions and fixes land in days, not weeks.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications):

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.

Hands-on experience with ECU instrumentation, calibration tooling, or embedded hardware integration (automotive or similar domain); experience level is flexible.

Practical experience with calibration/instrumentation tools such as INCA or similar environments and related measurement/flash tooling.

Familiarity with XCP (CAN/Ethernet/DoIP), UDS, or related measurement and diagnostic communication protocols.

Ability to read and interpret ECU schematics, interface documents, and instrumentation add-on boards, and to identify issues that affect bench usability.

Experience working with microcontroller-based ECU hardware and lab environments (benches, harnesses, trace connectors, power supplies, etc.)

Knowledgeable about industry standards for instrumentation, such as ASAM (ASAP-3, MCD-3MC, MCD-2MC, MCD-1 XCP) and Nexus 5001 (IEEE-ISTO 5001, JTAG, Aurora).

Strong troubleshooting skills across hardware, software, and tooling, with the ability to isolate issues and drive them to closure.

Strong attention to detail around versions, configurations, and controller/instrumentation variants across multiple ECUs and architectures.

Clear, concise communication skills and the ability to work directly with SWILs, calibrators, hardware engineers, and external partners.

Willingness to spend regular time on benches and in labs, working directly on real hardware.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications):

5+ years of experience in ECU instrumentation, calibration tools, embedded hardware integration, or SDV-related infrastructure work.

Deep, hands-on experience with calibration and measurement environments (e.g., INCA-class tools), high-speed ETK/XETK-style hardware, and ECU flashing workflows.

Experience enabling or supporting XCP on DoIP, including security unlock strategies and integration of security utilities into measurement and calibration toolchains.

Experience with Lauterbach debugging hardware, TRACE32, and PRACTICE scripting.

Familiarity with trace/debug tools and associated scripting workflows for MCU-based controllers.

Experience creating or owning instrumentation/tooling requirement documents for ECU programs.

Proficiency with scripting (e.g., Python) or basic automation to streamline instrumentation workflows and checks.

Demonstrated ability to turn tribal instrumentation knowledge into clear, reusable guides and training.

5 weeks paid classroom training in Indianapolis, IN, all travel expenses paid. 8 to 10 weeks of mentorship in the field back home; followed by another 5 weeks paid classroom training in Indianapolis.

Further hands-on training by one of our technicians and a full-time job with us as a Mobile Diesel Mechanic in your market.

Real pay rates that you can afford to pay rent with and a predefined pathway for raises.

ABOUT US

We are a technology services company dedicated to helping organizations build and deploy cutting-edge AI solutions. From generative AI and custom LLM integrations to predictive analytics and intelligent automation, we work across industries to bring real-world AI applications to life. Our projects combine deep technical expertise with hands-on client collaboration to solve high-impact problems.


JOB SUMMARY

The Senior AI Deployment Manager, Finance brings strong finance-domain experience to client work that applies AI to accounting and finance workflows. You will lead client discovery and delivery workstreams, turn unclear process needs into a practical implementation plan, and partner with Forward Deployed Engineers to move the work forward.

The priority areas are order-to-cash, month-end accounting close, and procure-to-pay. You should understand how finance teams operate and have implemented AI workflows in real work. Deep accounting process judgment matters more than AI specialization; you should be able to learn new tools quickly, explain their limits, and bring engineering in where technical decisions require it.

Eliza works AI-first and expects everyone in the company to use AI tools thoughtfully in their work. Client priorities move quickly, and the work can be ambiguous. You will receive ownership of a workstream, not a fixed script, and will be expected to communicate risks and tradeoffs early.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


1. LEAD FINANCE DISCOVERY AND PROCESS MAPPING

 - Run client sessions to understand the finance outcome, users, current process, systems, data, controls, exceptions, and pain points.

 - Focus discovery on O2C, month-end close, and P2P; establish the facts needed to assess value and feasibility.

 - Identify which process steps are suitable for AI, where conventional automation is a better fit, and where human judgment must remain.


2. DEFINE A PRACTICAL IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

 - Translate finance needs into product requirements, prioritized MVP scope, acceptance criteria, and a work plan an FDE can build against.

 - Make dependencies, access needs, data quality, risks, and assumptions explicit.

 - Recommend a sequence that balances business value, feasibility, timing, and quality.


3. OWN THE DELIVERY WORKSTREAM

 - Manage scope, milestones, client decisions, risks, handoffs, and status through testing and client review.

 - Partner closely with an FDE, keeping business requirements and technical decisions aligned without taking over engineering ownership.

 - Evaluate workflow performance using agreed test cases and success criteria; surface failure modes and propose next steps.


4. BUILD CLIENT CONFIDENCE AND ADOPTION

 - Facilitate working sessions with finance SMEs and communicate progress and tradeoffs in clear language.

 - Present concise updates that distinguish verified results from estimates or hypotheses.

 - Help client teams understand the workflow, its limitations, review requirements, and operational handoffs.


5. CONTRIBUTE TO THE FINANCE DELIVERY PRACTICE

 - Support finance-focused pursuits and scope discussions with grounded process and implementation judgment.

 - Coach Associates or teammates on client delivery and finance-workstream execution where assigned.

 - Package reusable discovery questions, process maps, requirements patterns, and delivery lessons.


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - Strong finance-domain experience in finance transformation, program finance, corporate finance, or a related field.

 - Practical knowledge of at least one of order-to-cash, month-end close, or procure-to-pay. Experience in AP/AR, invoicing, ERP, or finance systems is relevant.

 - Evidence of implementing AI-supported workflows in real work; casual AI tool use alone is not enough.

 - Ability to lead client-facing discovery and delivery, structure ambiguous problems, and own work through measurable review.

 - Can translate finance process requirements into clear implementation considerations and partner effectively with engineers.

 - Working understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, with sound judgment about human review and operational risk.

 - Strong writing, presentation, stakeholder management, and prioritization skills.


PREFERRED

 - Finance transformation consulting or professional-services delivery experience.

 - FP&A, program finance, or analytical experience.

 - Controller, CPA, or accounting-operations background.

 - ERP implementation, finance automation, or finance-focused AI product experience.

 - Experience in a PE-backed company.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation (base salary + performance incentives tied to client outcomes).

 - Equity options in a growing AI services company.

 - Exposure to a wide range of industries and high-impact AI problems.

 - Travel opportunities for on-site client engagements (if desired)

 - Direct client ownership of finance AI work from discovery through implementation planning and outcome review.

 - Close partnership with engineers and finance leaders on real operational problems.

 - The opportunity to shape reusable methods for finance AI delivery.

 - Variety across finance processes, systems, and client environments.

 - A high-ownership role with room to grow as the OCFO practice develops.

Job Description:
The Registered Nurse (RN) is a professional caregiver who assumes responsibility and accountability for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating the care of patients. The staff RN utilizes the nursing process by use of technology, therapeutic intervention, evidence-based practice and coordination of care with other health team members.
Essential Functions

Assess: Performs appropriate assessment of physical, social, and psychological status (including cognitive, communicative, and developmental skills as appropriate). Seeks and evaluates information acquired from other members of interdisciplinary team: patient, family, physician, non-nursing disciplines, support staff, others.

Northrop Grumman Space Systems is seeking a Principal or Sr Principal Electromechanical Engineer to join our team. This position will be based out of Aurora, Colorado.

The selected candidate for this role will bring a strong background in computer hardware design and integration, with a focus on understanding how changes in requirements impact hardware designs. This role will involve working on systems that utilize diverse electrical signals including power, RF, and fiber optics.

A successful candidate will have experience that includes hardware design, integration, and functionality verification.

The selected candidate will be someone who can successfully:

Collaborate on the design and integration of hardware systems ensuring adherence to changing requirements and specifications.

Finalize/update drawings, support equipment moves, rack and stack of equipment and integration of computer equipment into a shelter for deployment.

Experience/interest in power/cooling or site construction and traveling to support installation and configuration events would be a plus.

CONUS and OCONUS travel possible.

Participate in system-level testing and verification processes, ensuring hardware meets all specified requirements and standards.

Conduct troubleshooting and modifications on existing hardware designs to enhance performance and reliability.

Utilize clear technical writing to document design alterations, prepare status reports, and develop design specifications and validation plans.

Maintain a proactive attitude in meetings with cross-functional teams, demonstrating initiative and professionalism while engaging with colleagues and stakeholders.

Position may require occasional travel to support field activities and hardware deployment.

 

This position can be staffed at either a Principal or Sr Principal level based on the basic qualifications below.

Basic Qualifications

Principal Electromechanical Engineer: 5 Years with Bachelors in Science STEM; 3 Years with Masters; 1 Year with PhD

Sr. Principal Electromechanical Engineer: 8 Years with Bachelors in Science STEM; 6 Years with Masters; 4 Years with PhD

Must have an active U.S. Government Top Secret security clearance at time of application, current and within scope, with the ability to obtain and maintain SCI approval/access.

Experience with hardware design and integration processes.

Demonstrated knowledge of the impacts of requirement changes on hardware design.

Familiarity with power, RF, and fiber electrical signal principles and applications.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with complex system architectures and hardware validation procedures.

Knowledge of electronic components and their applications in communication systems.

Previous experience in a fast-paced engineering environment with a focus on field support operations is desirable.

Primary Level Salary Range: $114,000.00 - $171,000.00

Secondary Level Salary Range: $142,200.00 - $213,400.00

The Chief of Staff (CoS) serves as a senior executive, strategic advisor, and operational partner to the Regional CEO. Working across Business Units, Group functions, and Centres of Excellence, this senior-level role drives strategic alignment, governance, operational execution, and organizational effectiveness to enable the successful delivery of the business portfolio's growth, product, health, and market transformation ambitions.

The role acts as a trusted executive partner, ensuring leadership focus on critical priorities, accelerating decision-making, removing barriers to execution, fostering collaboration across markets and functions, and translating enterprise priorities into measurable business outcomes. Supported by dedicated executive administrative support, the Chief of Staff focuses strictly on high-impact strategic content, enterprise performance, and operational governance.

Key Responsibilities

 

Strategic Advisor to Regional CEO

Serve as a trusted thought partner to the Regional CEO on strategic, commercial, and organizational priorities.

Support the development and execution of the business portfolio’s strategy and annual operating plan.

Provide insights, rigorous analysis, and actionable recommendations to support executive decision-making.

Anticipate emerging risks, opportunities, and market developments that could impact business performance across regions and global pillars.

Ensure strategic priorities are translated into actionable execution plans across Local Business Units (LBUs).

Act as a sounding board on business, talent, governance, and transformation matters.

 

Drive Strategic Execution and Transformation

 

Lead and coordinate critical strategic initiatives sponsored by the Regional CEO, with dedicated emphasis on driving progress across Group Product and Group Health growth pillars.

Monitor delivery of transformation, growth, product expansion, and capability-building programmes across Indonesia, the Philippines, and Africa.

Ensure timely execution of Group strategic initiatives across markets and functional matrix lines.

Establish clear governance, milestones, and accountability mechanisms for key projects.

Identify execution risks and implement mitigation actions to maintain momentum.

Track outcomes and ensure benefits realization from major investments and transformation programmes.

 

Business Performance Management

Partner directly with Local Business Units (LBU) CEOs, Chief Strategy and Transformation Officers (CSTOs), and functional leaders to monitor and drive business performance.

Actively lean in and take a hands-on, problem-solving role when markets or strategic pillars face performance headwinds or execution challenges.

Drive performance management disciplines across growth, financial, and operational metrics.

Synthesize actionable insights from markets to inform leadership decisions and strategic course corrections.

Lead quarterly business reviews, operating reviews, and executive business planning processes on behalf of the Regional CEO.

Develop dashboards, performance reporting, and forecasting frameworks to improve transparency and decision quality.

Coordinate and structure preparations for Board, Group, investor, and executive performance discussions.

 

Executive Governance and Leadership Effectiveness

Shape agendas and desired outcomes for regional leadership forums, executive committees, and governance meetings.

Ensure high-quality decision papers and rigorous follow-through on agreed actions.

Coordinate and monitor commitments and strategic priorities across the region.

Facilitate effective governance processes and stakeholder engagement across the business.

Improve organizational focus by ensuring leadership attention is concentrated on high-value priorities.

Support the Regional CEO in managing leadership team effectiveness and operating rhythm.

 

Cross-Functional and Cross-Market Leadership

Build strong partnerships across Local Business Units (LBUs), Group Functions, Centres of Excellence, and enabling functions.

Align stakeholders around common priorities and enterprise objectives, facilitating close alignment with LBU leadership to land regional strategy into effective local implementation.

Break down organizational silos to improve collaboration and speed of execution.

Facilitate effective communication between markets, regional teams, and Group stakeholders.

Ensure markets receive timely support and escalation resolution from Group functions.

Foster best-practice sharing and synergies across the organizational ecosystem.

 

Communications and Stakeholder Engagement

Develop executive-level communications, strategic messaging, and leadership narratives.

Coordinate Regional CEO communications to leadership teams and broader employee populations.

Support employee engagement, culture, and organizational alignment initiatives.

Prepare executive presentations, speeches, briefing materials, and stakeholder updates.

Ensure clarity and consistency of messaging across strategic priorities.

Represent the Regional CEO in selected forums and engagements when required.

 

Organizational Effectiveness and Culture

Support initiatives that strengthen leadership alignment, employee engagement, and organizational health.

Drive initiatives that improve collaboration, trust, and cohesion across the enterprise.

Support talent, succession, and capability-building priorities across the region.

Champion Prudential values and leadership behaviours.

Promote inclusion, diversity, and sustainability initiatives where appropriate.

 

 

Experience and Qualifications

 

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Strategy, Actuarial Science, or related discipline.

Advanced degree (MBA or equivalent) preferred.

12+ years of experience in strategy, consulting, corporate finance, transformation, insurance, or banking.

Demonstrated success in leading complex cross-functional initiatives and driving end-to-end execution.

Strong understanding of business performance management and commercial/financial drivers.

Proven track record of working effectively with C-suite executives and senior leadership teams.

Exposure to regional or multinational business environments preferred.

Insurance and financial services experience is highly desirable.

Preferred Attributes

 

Core Triad: Exceptional blend of sharp strategic thinking, a proven track record of operational execution, and deep financial acumen.

Hands-on Execution: Ability to seamlessly alternate between high-level enterprise strategy and deep-dive operational problem-solving in underperforming areas.

Stakeholder Impact: Exceptional stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence without formal authority and navigate complex matrix organizational dynamics.

Matrix Alignment: Ability to support the Regional CEO in driving Group-wide strategy across Local Business Units (LBUs), working closely with LBUs Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy & Transformation Officer to translate strategy into high-impact local implementation.

Agility & Presence: Executive presence, intellectual curiosity, and the confidence to constructively challenge senior leaders while operating effectively amid ambiguity and pace.

Communication: Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex commercial and functional issues for executive leadership.

Job Overview

As a Customer Experience Colleague, you will create exceptional, personalized shopping experiences for our customers. You’ll prioritize customer satisfaction by actively engaging with shoppers across all touchpoints - both in-store and online - and drive cross-category sales to support overall business goals. With a deep understanding of fashion, fit, and function, you will make tailored product recommendations and leverage digital tools to enhance the customer journey. You also will work across different departments daily, often transitioning between multiple areas throughout the day.

In this role, you’ll also play a key part in client relationship building through outreach tools like My Client and social media. Your collaborative approach with peers, store leaders, and brand partners will help identify opportunities, resolve challenges, and elevate the overall customer experience. In addition to service and selling, you’ll support operational excellence through floor readiness, event execution, merchandise setup, and opening/closing procedures.

A positive, can-do attitude, strong communication skills, and a passion for delivering high-caliber service will be key to your success in this role.

How Our Selling Colleagues Spend Their Day...

Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They wear their name badge with pride, greet teammates with a warm hello, and help ensure the sales floor is clean, organized, and prepared for customers. Before getting started, they review their sales goals, learn about new arrivals and top-selling items, and stay up to date on current trends and promotions - so they’re fully informed and ready to engage, educate, and sell with confidence.
On the floor, they focus on the customer - offering a warm welcome, making eye contact, and creating friendly, personal conversations to create customer relationships to bring the customers back.
Throughout the day, they maintain a shoppable space by recovering the floor and fitting rooms, updating signs and pricing, and supporting any needed merchandise moves.
They always Finish Strong - sharing our Loyalty program benefits, making sure customers have all they need, and ending with a sincere thank-you, often walking the package around and using the customer’s name.
We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

The North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources (DNCR) enriches people’s lives through education and stewardship of North Carolina’s natural and cultural resources. DNCR manages over 100 locations across the state, including historic sites, museums, state parks, trails, aquariums, the North Carolina Zoo, the Library of North Carolina, the State Archives, the North Carolina Arts Council, the African American Heritage Commission, the American Indian Heritage Commission, the State Historic Preservation Office, the Office of State Archaeology, the Highway Historical Markers program, the North Carolina Land and Water Fund, and the Natural Heritage Program. Manage and mitigate risks through assessment, in support of the control and governance agenda.

Demonstrate leadership and accountability for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work your team does.

Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the organisation functions to contribute to achieving the goals of the business.

Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategies.

Create solutions based on sophisticated analytical thought comparing and selecting complex alternatives. In-depth analysis with interpretative thinking will be required to define problems and develop innovative solutions.

Adopt and include the outcomes of extensive research in problem solving processes.

Seek out, build and maintain trusting relationships and partnerships with internal and external stakeholders in order to accomplish key business objectives, using influencing and negotiating skills to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

Overall Purpose of Role

The Senior Regional Economist will be responsible for leading Barclays' economic research coverage of Emerging Asia, with primary responsibility for North Asian economies, including South Korea and Taiwan. The role will involve developing independent macroeconomic views, forecasting key economic and market variables, analysing central bank and government policy developments, and communicating investment implications to institutional investors and internal stakeholders.

The successful candidate will work closely with economists, strategists, sales and trading teams across the globe to deliver differentiated research and actionable insights. The role requires strong analytical capabilities, excellent written and verbal communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to engage with senior institutional investors and policymakers.

This role is open to be based in Singapore / Hong Kong.

Key Accountabilities

Lead economic research coverage of Emerging Asia, with particular focus on South Korea and Taiwan.

Develop proprietary macroeconomic forecasts covering growth, inflation, labour markets, fiscal policy, monetary policy and external sector dynamics.

Monitor and analyse regional central bank decisions, government policy initiatives, geopolitical developments and structural economic trends.

Produce timely research reports, thematic publications and market commentaries for institutional investors.

Generate differentiated investment insights and translate macroeconomic developments into implications for rates, FX, equities and credit markets.

Collaborate closely with Global Economics, FX Strategy, Rates Strategy and Equity Research teams to ensure consistency of views and integrated client solutions.

Represent Barclays Research through client meetings, conferences, webinars, roadshows and media engagements where appropriate.

Develop and maintain relationships with policymakers, regulatory bodies, industry participants and academic institutions across the region.

Contribute to franchise development through innovative research themes and thought leadership initiatives.

Mentor junior economists and research staff while fostering a collaborative research culture.

Essential Skills and Experience

Advanced degree in Economics, Econometrics, Public Policy, Finance or a related quantitative discipline. PhD preferred.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Korean language capabilities are advantageous.

Significant experience covering Asian economies within a leading investment bank, research institution, central bank, international organisation or policy institution.

Deep knowledge of the economies of South Korea and Taiwan, including monetary policy frameworks and political economy considerations.

Strong forecasting, econometric and quantitative analytical capabilities.

Proven track record of publishing high-quality macroeconomic research and investment-relevant insights.

Excellent presentation and communication skills, with experience engaging directly with institutional investors and senior stakeholders.

Strong understanding of global macro, rates and foreign exchange markets.

Ability to influence outcomes through collaboration and intellectual leadership.

Demonstrated commercial awareness and ability to identify themes that create value for clients.

Preferred Experience

Existing relationships with regional policymakers, regulators, and market participants.

Experience presenting at major investor conferences and media events.

Familiarity with North Asia regional dynamics.

You may be assessed on key critical skills relevant for success in the role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking, as well as job-specific technical skills.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. The Lead IT Architect serves as the strategic architecture leader across multiple products and value streams within the Specialty technology portfolio. This role is responsible for defining and driving architecture direction, enabling scalable growth, improving platform reuse, and ensuring technical investments align with business objectives. 

The position works across engineering, product, and business stakeholders to establish architecture standards, support strategic planning activities, and guide technology decisions that impact multiple teams and products. The Lead IT Architect plays an active role in program increment (PI) planning, architectural runway development, and long-term technology strategy, helping teams balance immediate delivery needs with future scalability and modernization. 

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, portfolio-level technology governance, and healthcare technology environments. While artificial intelligence is not the primary focus of the position, candidates should be comfortable evaluating AI-enabled capabilities, supporting AI feature development, and establishing appropriate architecture guidance for AI-related solutions.  

Key Responsibilities 

Define and maintain the architecture vision, roadmap, an technical strategy across multiple products and value streams. 

Partner with product, engineering, and business leaders to align technology investments with organizational priorities. 

Provide architectural leadership for cross-product initiatives, shared services, integration patterns, and platform capabilities. 

Establish and govern architecture standards, design principles, and reusable technology patterns. 

Lead architecture discussions and decision-making during strategic planning and PI planning activities. 

Develop and maintain the architectural runway required to support future business and technology objectives. 

Guide the design of distributed, cloud-native solutions utilizing APIs, event-driven architectures, microservices, and modern integration patterns. 

Drive consistency across products by identifying opportunities for platform reuse and reducing duplicated technology investments. 

Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture and shared-service organizations to ensure alignment with broader technology strategies. 

Provide architectural oversight for third-party vendors, implementation partners, and systems integrators. 

Ensure solutions support healthcare compliance, data privacy, security, and interoperability requirements. 

Mentor architects, senior engineers, and technical leaders to strengthen architecture practices and technical decision-making across the organization. 

Evaluate emerging technologies and AI-enabled capabilities, providing guidance on appropriate adoption and implementation within the portfolio. 

 
Priority will be given to candidates residing in the Columbus, OH metropolitan area. 

 

We are unable to provide sponsorship for this role, presently or in the future. 

 

Minimum Qualifications  

Degree or equivalent and typically requires 10+ years of relevant experience. Less years required if has relevant Master’s or Doctorate qualifications. 

 

Critical Skills 

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. 

12+ years of experience in architecture, software engineering, or senior technical leadership roles. 

8+ years of experience working within software development organizations and modern delivery environments. 

3+ years of experience defining architecture strategy across multiple products, platforms, programs, or value streams. 

Experience establishing and governing architecture standards adopted by independent product or engineering teams. 

Demonstrated success designing and delivering large-scale distributed systems and cloud-native solutions. 

Experience with microservices, RESTful APIs, event-driven architectures, and enterprise integration patterns. 

Experience developing architecture roadmaps and managing architectural dependencies across multiple teams. 

Experience presenting technology strategies, recommendations, and tradeoffs to senior leadership. 

 
 

Preferred Qualifications 

Experience within healthcare, pharmacy, payer, provider, or other regulated technology environments. 

Experience participating in large-scale planning activities and translating business strategy into technology roadmaps. 

Experience designing systems that manage regulated or sensitive data. 

Working knowledge of healthcare interoperability and compliance standards, including FHIR and HIPAA. 

Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions across teams without direct management authority. 

Experience working within SAFe or other scaled agile frameworks. 

Knowledge of NCPDP standards and healthcare interoperability ecosystems. 

Experience creating shared platforms or reusable enterprise capabilities used across multiple product teams. 

Experience overseeing architecture deliverables from vendors, consulting partners, or systems integrators. 

Familiarity with AI-enabled product features, AI-assisted development tools, and governance considerations related to AI adoption. 

Experience mentoring architects and developing architecture communities of practice. 

 
 

What Success Looks Like 

Within the first 12 months, the successful candidate will: 

Establish a clear architecture vision and roadmap across supported products and value streams. 

Improve alignment and consistency of architectural decisions across teams. 

Increase adoption of reusable platforms, shared services, and architectural standards. 

Reduce technical duplication and improve long-term scalability across the portfolio. 

Create stronger alignment between strategic business priorities, PI planning activities, and technology investments. 

Serve as a trusted architecture advisor to engineering, product, and business leadership. 

Introduce practical guidance for evaluating and implementing AI-enabled capabilities where they create measurable business value. 

 
 

Why This Role Is Unique 

This is not a product-level solution architecture role. The Lead IT Architect operates at the portfolio level, influencing architecture direction across multiple products and value streams. The role combines strategic planning, architecture governance, technology leadership, and business alignment, giving the successful candidate an opportunity to shape the future technology direction of a critical healthcare platform while working closely with senior leaders across the organization.

Job Description
 

Overview

The Development Manager manages, oversees, coordinates, and provides direction for all development activities for the department. Manages the provision of Sustainable Development and Construction and all programs, permitting, processes, and administration.

Position Note:
